key_insight: A five-qubit hybrid quantum neural network achieved 55.4–59.8% suspicious-class F1 on IBM hardware, but classical XGBoost remained best at 61.4%.
engineering_relevance: Compact hybrid circuits merit further benchmarking for trade surveillance, though these results do not establish quantum advantage or production readiness.
method: Compare four quantum or hybrid classifiers with logistic regression, XGBoost, neural networks and classical KNN.
Use shared stratified train/test splits and 20-feature ANOVA and PCA representations.
Test QKNN and QSVM under simulated noise and deploy the five-qubit hybrid model on ibm_fez.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 1,000 synthetic accounts, with 800 for training, 200 for testing and 20% suspicious; the hardware hybrid model outperformed six of eight classical configurations.
watch_item: A single split of a small synthetic dataset limits confidence in generalization to real-world surveillance.
paper_title: Hybrid Quantum Algorithms for Trade Surveillance Analytics
